This worked example takes one flip-chip Xmon qubit through both solvers. This
page builds its plan and prepares it as `snapshot`; the
[Palace page](palace.qmd) and the [AEDT page](aedt.qmd) start from it, in the
same Python session. The plan holds this model:

![The flip-chip Xmon as the plan prepares it. Left: the face of the upper chip (D1) that faces the lower chip, to scale: the cross-shaped Xmon pad, 309.5 µm from tip to tip with 24.65 µm wide arms, four couplers 20 µm from its tips, the ground plane around them, and eight indium bumps that join the two chips' ground planes. The red mark is the junction sheet between the pad and the ground plane. Right: the layer stack, not to scale; the two chips face each other across an 8.2 µm vacuum gap.](../../assets/xmon-flip-chip.png){#fig-xmon-flip-chip}

Two silicon chips, each 500 µm thick, face each other. The lower chip (D0)
carries a ground plane on its top face; the upper chip (D1) carries the Xmon
on the face turned down towards it. Eight indium bumps, each 20 µm square,
connect the two ground planes across the 8.2 µm gap. The model is 1060 µm
square. The junction is modelled by its sheet, a small sheet that joins the pad
to the D1 ground plane: both backend pages put an 11.78 nH inductor
there, the value of the PDK's public notebooks for this qubit.

You need SCGSim with its `palace` extra for the Palace page or its `aedt-epr`
extra for the AEDT page, and the OrcaPen SC PDK
([Install SCGSim](../../start/install.qmd)).

## Draw the coupon {#build-the-component-and-named-coupon-occurrences}

```python
import gdsfactory as gf
import orcapen_sc_pdk
from orcapen_sc_pdk import LAYER_STACK, get_material_records
from orcapen_sc_pdk.helpers.assembly import place_flip_chip_ground_short_bumps
from orcapen_sc_pdk.tech import OUTER_VACUUM_THICKNESS_UM
from scgsim.geometry import GeometryPlan

orcapen_sc_pdk.activate()
gf.clear_cache()
device = gf.get_component(
    "kosen2024_flip_chip_xmon_qubit",
    bump_ring_count_per_side=0,
    qubit_pad_length=309.5,
    qubit_pad_width=24.65,
    qubit_gap=20.0,
)
coupon = place_flip_chip_ground_short_bumps(
    device,
    coupon_padding_um=75.0,
    clearance_um=30.0,
    placement_mode="corner_anchors",
)
component = coupon.component
```

`kosen2024_flip_chip_xmon_qubit` draws the Xmon, its four couplers and its
junction sheet; `bump_ring_count_per_side=0` leaves out the device's own
rings of bumps. `place_flip_chip_ground_short_bumps` puts it in a coupon, the
small piece of the chip that is simulated: it adds the two ground planes and
the eight shorting bumps, two at each corner. The coupon names each placed
part: `device` for the Xmon and `short_000` to `short_007` for the bumps.

## Make the plan {#assign-the-final-net-map-and-prepare-one-snapshot}

```python
plan = GeometryPlan(
    component=component,
    root_id="chip",
    layer_stack=LAYER_STACK,
    material_records=get_material_records(),
    coupon_padding_um=coupon.stack_coupon_padding_um,
)
for name, reference in coupon.named_instances.items():
    plan.register_instance(f"chip/{name}", reference)

plan.set_nets({
    "xmon_pad": ("chip/device/D1_XMON_PAD",),
    "Ground": (
        "chip/D0_TOP_GROUND_PLANE",
        "chip/D1_BOTTOM_GROUND_PLANE",
        *(f"chip/device/D1_COUPLER_{index}" for index in range(1, 5)),
        *(
            f"chip/{name}/D0_D1_INDIUM_BUMP"
            for name in coupon.named_instances
            if name.startswith("short_")
        ),
    ),
})
plan.set_vacuum_region(
    padding=(0.0, 0.0, float(OUTER_VACUUM_THICKNESS_UM))
)
snapshot = plan.prepare()
port_name = "chip/device/o_junction_lumped"
```

What each step fixes:

- `LAYER_STACK` is the PDK's two-chip stack of the figure, and
  `coupon.stack_coupon_padding_um` the substrate margin the coupon helper
  chose around the layout.
- `register_instance` gives each placed part its name in the plan, so that
  its shapes are found under `chip/device/...` and `chip/short_000/...`.
  Each named shape is an Entity.
- `set_nets` groups the Entities into Nets, each a named piece of metal that
  acts as one conductor:

  | Net | Entities |
  |---|---|
  | `xmon_pad` | the Xmon pad, `chip/device/D1_XMON_PAD` |
  | `Ground` | both ground planes, the four couplers and the eight bumps |

  The couplers are grounded here because the example has no readout or
  drive line; in a device with them, they would be Nets of their own.
- `set_vacuum_region` adds 1000 µm of vacuum above and below the two chips
  (`OUTER_VACUUM_THICKNESS_UM`) and none beyond their sides. The 8.2 µm gap
  between the chips is part of the stack, not of this region.
- `port_name` is the junction sheet's name in the plan; both backend pages use
  it.

## Next {#observe-the-prepared-source-and-continue}

Continue with [Flip-chip Xmon with Palace](palace.qmd) or
[Flip-chip Xmon with AEDT](aedt.qmd) in the same session. To look at what the
plan holds before you simulate, see [Inspect the source](../inspect-the-source.qmd);
the [GeometryPlan reference](../../reference/specs/geometry-plan.qmd#component-to-backend-geometry-contract)
gives the rules for placed parts, Entities and Nets.

The Xmon cell is OrcaPen's own parametric adaptation of the qubit of Kosen
et al., [PRX Quantum 5, 030350 (2024)](https://doi.org/10.1103/PRXQuantum.5.030350),
shared under [CC BY 4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/); it is
not the authors' mask, and its dimensions are example inputs, not measured
device data. The [PDK's notebooks for this qubit](https://github.com/NCUPHY-LTLab/orcapen-sc-pdk/tree/49e539fd59f3224ecda965d777c7ec3aadcc3b85/notebooks/src/ComponentSimulation/Kosen2024_Xmon)
are the source of its settings.
